question: Should experimental Claws be permitted to register arbitrary stdio MCP commands and reuse globally named MCP declarations, or must both actions be mediated by an explicit host authorization policy?
rationale: This is a permanent execution and cross-resource ownership contract; source-level mechanical changes cannot safely choose the allowed command set, environment policy, or sharing model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Broker and authorize MCP resources
options.body: Require a host-approved or brokered stdio command path, explicit environment policy, and host authorization before sharing a global MCP declaration.

options.title: Pause the MCP ownership stage
options.body: Keep this stage out of the landing stack until the RFC or maintainers establish the execution and global-resource ownership contract.

recommendation.title: Broker and authorize MCP resources
recommendation.body: Require a host-approved or brokered stdio command path, explicit environment policy, and host authorization before sharing a global MCP declaration.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned and has already identified the two unresolved contract boundaries in detailed review.
